intro.title: Build typed filter and sort state model
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a typed state model to manage filter and sort options for a list of items. You'll learn how to use TypeScript interfaces to define the shape of your state, ensuring type safety for properties like filter criteria and sort order. The core concept involves modeling application state with explicit types to prevent errors and improve code clarity. You'll work with TypeScript constructs such as interfaces and type annotations to create a robust, maintainable state structure.
intro.usecase: This pattern is essential for building interactive data interfaces like e-commerce product filters, admin dashboards with sorting controls, or analytics panels with user-configurable views. Developers implement typed filter and sort state models to manage user selections for categories, price ranges, or date periods while ensuring data consistency and type safety. For example, a real estate listing site uses this model to let users filter by property type, bedrooms, and location, then sort by price or date—all with compile-time validation preventing runtime errors. Mastering this approach allows you to create robust, maintainable filtering systems that scale with complex application requirements.
